agree.reason: This reader has lost money before and is wary of first-time creators, so the honest tone and the factory quote would reassure them a little, but there is no delivery date, no refund promise and no update schedule, and the empty placeholders make the page look unfinished, so they would probably hold back.

honest.reason: The draft rightly avoids calling the game a 'proven hit', but it adds unsupported claims: 'from families to veteran gamers', 'every one of those sessions changed something', 'works just as well' solo, and 'the only way this game gets printed'; it also calls the raters 'early players' rather than saying most of them played at the designer's own convention table.

works_the_facts.reason: It lists the raw figures but derives nothing from them: it never shows that the goal needs about 571 backers at $49 (about 46% of the 1,240 sign-ups), or that at the goal the costs come to about $25,300 (the $17,400 quote, about $5,100 shipping and about $2,800 in fees), which leaves roughly a $2,700 buffer.

right_comparison.reason: The only alternative it gives is the invented claim that the game won't be printed without crowdfunding, and it never compares backing this project with the risk the reader knows from first-time campaigns that failed to deliver.

qualification.reason: The only hedge is a vague promise of 'honest updates throughout', with no checkable commitment such as November delivery, an update every two weeks, or a full refund if delivery is more than three months late.

objections.reason: It names the first-time-creator concern and mentions the factory quote, but it leaves out the answers that would settle it: the finished art and rules, the signed quote, the delivery date, the refund promise, the update schedule and the reviewer's launch-week video.

fit.reason: It is a pitch of about 500 words, as asked, but key parts are still placeholders: the game title, the description of a turn, international shipping and the creator's name.
